item.title: Its A Game
item.description: “You are not in a fight at all really. The only person you are fighting is yourself, not your opponent. It isn’t even a fight, it’s a game. The game is positional advantage. Incrementally improve your with every movement or engagement, and never give it up. Then you will have your opponent controlled and in position to apply a submission.” - Gabriel Rainho, renown Jiu Jitsu coach and competitor, comment made to me Nov 2025, post grading. Check him out for more tips, words of wisdom and some amazing submission! Gabriel Rainho Instagram. For some more wise words, and a nasty sub: https://www.instagram.com/p/DWqQHJZCMaU/

item.title: Ppppppp
item.description: “It’s certainly not a war for which they prepared. I think it illustrates one of the important themes of my work with Stephen Broadberry, which is that the people who go into war often underestimate the range of options open to the adversary. You know, they think they’re going to win a crushing victory in a few weeks, but they don’t take into account that the incentive for the adversary is always to think outside the box, and that’s what Iranian leaders have done.” Source: From The Economics Show: Economic warfare: lessons from history, with Mark Harrison, 2 Apr 2026 https://podcasts.apple.com/ca/podcast/the-economics-show/id1746352576?i=1000758774803&r=295

item.title: Careful What You Measure
item.description: “The more any quantitative social indicator is used for social decision-making, the more subject it will be to corruption pressures and the more apt it will be to distort and corrupt the social processes it is intended to monitor” - Source: Campbell’s Law (American social scientist Donald T Campbell), circa 9171. Just switch social science for government or corporate policy and you will have the gist of it.

item.title: Its A You Problem
item.description:
“In the British Army, there are no good battalions and no bad battalions, no good regiments and no bad regiments. There are only good and bad officers.” - General Slim. Defeat into Victory is an account of the retaking of Burma by Allied forces during the Second World War by the British Field Marshal William Slim.

This is the same as the Napoleon quote of “No poor soldiers, only poor officers”, which is the same concept of only poor workers blame their tools. The wider extrapolation here is that if it goes wrong, you have to own it. It is, quite literally, a ‘you’ problem. Even if the staff are incompetent, it can only be so because you tolerated incompetence or you hired the incompetent.

item.title: Approxmimately Right
item.description: “It’s better to be approximately right than precisely wrong.” - Warren Buffet. Keynes? Many people over time. Warren made it stick though. Original source is 1898 book by Carveth Read, a British author in philosophy and logic, Logic: Deductive and Inductive (1898 – first edition). In chapter 22 the author writes: “It is better to be vaguely right than exactly wrong” (Read, 1898, p. 351). It’s there, I checked. I can also spell (mostly), the title is to make the point. https://www.gutenberg.org/files/18440/18440-h/18440-h.htm

item.title: The Cold Never Lasts
item.description: “The cold never lasts, my darling. It just teaches the heart how to burn”. - Raye. Click Clack Symphony from the albumn This Music May Contain Hope. 2026.

item.title: Dont Start What You Cant Finish
item.description: “The guerrilla wins if he does not lose. The conventional army loses if he does not win”. Henry Kissinger, 1969 Foriegn Affairs. Beware the asymetry of non conventional conflicts. Don’t start what you haven’t the stomach to see through to the better end. War should be an all or nothing committment. Nothing is a good choice most of the time. But in between may lie intelligent battles to ensure the attrition of the capacity of your enemy.

item.title: Not All Relationships Are Positive
item.description: “high genetic homozygosity,” is probably a bad thing. Consider adjusting your life plans aligned to this.

item.title: The Rise Of The Machine
item.description: You are only what the system says you are. Beware the rise of the machine. I write this reading an article on a UK born and bred midwife, facing immigration expulsion from Canada on grounds of a technical problem with the confirmation of her English language test. Yes, this is insane. Doubly so for forcing her to take the test in the first place. When no sane person within the system argues against blindly following “the rules”, we are all doomed. “We are sorry you are dissatisfied with our service today, the system says you are scheduled for Euthanasia. Your complaint is now set to ‘resolved’. Please enjoy your day.”

item.title: Bowie On Work
item.description: Games are a series of interesting choices. Never play to the gallery, but you never learn that until much later on. Never work for other people. Always remember that the reason you initially started working was that there was something inside yourself that you felt that if you could manifest it in some way, you would understand more about yourself and how you coexist with the rest of society. It is terribly dangerous for an artist to fulfil other people’s expectations. They generally produce their worst work when they do that. — David Bowie

item.title: Constrained Distribution

item.title: Josephus On Drills
item.description: “Their drills are bloodless battles, and their battles bloody drills.” — Josephus, The Jewish War, 3.5.1. Their military exercises differ not at all from the real use of their arms, but every soldier is every day exercised, and that with great diligence, as if it were in time of war, which is the reason why they bear the fatigue of battles so easily.

item.title: What You Would Not
item.description: Never send someone else to do what you would not. Note not what you could not do, but what you would not do. We all have mixed skills and experiences. Your credibility rests on the point of courage. No one respects a REMF.
